prompt.query: Determine the mechanism of the following reaction: acetone self-aldol condensation -> mesityl oxide (4-methylpent-3-en-2-one). Reactant SMILES: [OH-].CC(=O)C.CC(=O)C; product SMILES: [OH-].CC(=O)C=C(C)C.O; total charge -1, multiplicity 1; conditions: NaOH or Ba(OH)2, heated. Atom-mapped reactant SMILES: [OH-:1].[CH:2]([H:3])([H:11])[C:4](=[O:5])[CH3:6].[CH3:7][C:8](=[O:9])[CH3:10]. The 1-based map numbers in it are the indexing convention for `bond_changes` (keep using the plain SMILES above for graph nodes and evidence annotations). The reaction may proceed through a multi-step network: represent each intermediate you identify as a node and each elementary step as an edge; competing pathways you investigate deserve their own edges. You must maintain `mechanism_graph.json` in the sandbox root recording the mechanism graph: nodes (reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state, with SMILES) and elementary-step edges (with `via` pointing to the TS node id). Start the graph at the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex), not at the separated reactants. The scorer checks that your graph covers the reference mechanism as a subgraph: extra nodes or edges beyond the reference are never penalized, so record every step you actually investigated. Every elementary-step edge must carry `bond_changes`: `break`/`form` lists of [i, j] atom-map index pairs, where [i, j] belongs to `break` if the bond order between atoms i and j decreases over the step (including full cleavage) and to `form` if it increases (including newly formed bonds); a purely conformational or inversion step carries two empty lists. The scorer reads this file forensically; a missing or unparseable file severely impacts the score. Every computational evidence file you produce for a species or step (QM input or log) must carry a `smiles: <SMILES>` comment line identifying the species, so the scorer can bind each graph element to concrete evidence. In your final summary you must report the computed barrier in kcal/mol for the rate-determining step, relative to the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex, e.g. the ion-dipole complex of a bimolecular reaction; for a unimolecular process this is simply the reactant minimum). Run the computations with ORCA or Gaussian: the scorer parses only these two programs' log formats, so output from any other program cannot count as evidence. Allowed computational methods are limited to MACE-OMol25 and xTB; calls beyond the whitelist are intercepted.

edges.step_type: enolate formation: OH- deprotonates the alpha-C of acetone (C=O pi shifts to C=C)
C-C addition: enolate carbon attacks the second acetone carbonyl -> diacetone alcohol alkoxide (capturable)
alkoxide reprotonation by water -> diacetone alcohol, regenerating OH-
E1cb deprotonation: OH- removes the alpha-H on the other side of the carbinol -> enolate + water
E1cb elimination: hydroxide leaves with C=C formation (enolate collapse), giving mesityl oxide
